{{Current events|year=2021|month=02|day=16|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Ma'rib Campaign]]
***[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces continue to advance on the city of [[Maʼrib]], capturing the village of al-Zor and reaching the [[Marib Dam]]. [[Yemeni government]] officials say that dozens of people have been killed in the past 24 hours as government forces counter the Houthi offensive. UN [[Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator]] [[Mark Lowcock]] condemns the Houthi assault, warning of "unimaginable humanitarian consequences". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/16/un-alarmed-as-battle-for-marib-threatens-millions-of-yemenis (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**A spokesperson for the rebel group [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] claimed that an estimated 100,000 troops (both Tigrayan and Ethiopian) have been killed during the conflict. Three Ethiopian opposition parties previously claimed that an estimated 52,000 civilians have also died. [https://www.eepa.be//wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Situation-Report-EEPA-Horn-No.-86-17-February-2021.pdf (Europe External Programme with Africa)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-02/ethiopian-opposition-claims-52-000-dead-in-northern-conflict (Bloomberg)]
**[[President of Rwanda|Rwandan President]] [[Paul Kagame]] stated that the reported deaths in Tigray were too high to let Ethiopia and the African Union handle the situation alone. He said that the UN should intervene in the Tigray War, explaining that when a state is not able to stop atrocities on its territory, such as genocide, the UN has a duty to intervene. [https://www.agenceecofin.com/gestion-publique/1602-85246-ethiopie-paul-kagame-appelle-a-une-action-directe-du-conseil-de-securite-de-l-onu-pour-resoudre-la-crise-dans-le-tigre (Agence Ecofin)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**[[New Zealand]] announces that it will withdraw its [[New Zealand Defence Force|forces]] from [[Afghanistan]] by May. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/436571/new-zealand-troops-to-be-withdrawn-from-afghanistan-by-may (Radio New Zealand)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[White House]] announces that [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] will extend the [[foreclosure]] ban and mortgage [[forbearance]] through the end of June as an effort to address the economic impact of the [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] pandemic. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/biden-extends-foreclosure-moratorium-mortgage-forbearance-through-june-n1257983 (NBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Tornadoes of 2021]]
**A tornado in [[Brunswick County, North Carolina|Brunswick County]], [[North Carolina]] kills 3 people and injures 10 others. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2021/02/16/brunswick-county-tornado-north-carolina/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2020–21 North American winter]]
**The [[February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm|Winter Storm Uri]] kills at least 23 people and causes power outages for millions of people across the United States. [https://nypost.com/2021/02/17/at-least-21-dead-as-brutal-cold-from-historic-storm-sweeps-across-us/ (''New York Post'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[First Minister of Scotland|First Minister]] [[Nicola Sturgeon]] confirms that a phased return to school will begin on February 22, which will include [[pre-school]] children, pupils in primaries 1, 2 and 3, and secondary students who need to carry out practical assignments. [https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/feb/16/sturgeon-schools-scotland-begin-phased-return-monday (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] receives 550,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/hungary-gets-first-shipment-of-chinas-sinopharm-vaccine/a-56586599 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]]'s first case of B.1525 [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] found in [[Naples]] in a person who had recently travelled from  a country in Africa. [https://www.thelocal.it/20210217/first-italian-case-of-rare-new-covid-variant-detected-in-naples (''The Local Italy'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports their first case of the [[501.V2 variant]] first detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/malta-records-first-case-of-south-africa-covid-19-variant.851942 (''Times of Malta'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
*****[[Massachusetts]] reports their first case of the [[501.V2 variant]] first detected in [[South Africa]] in a woman in her 20s from [[Middlesex County, Massachusetts|Middlesex County]]. [https://www.masslive.com/coronavirus/2021/02/first-case-of-the-south-african-covid-19-variant-confirmed-in-massachusetts-officials-announce.html (Masslive)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic]]
****The [[Dominican Republic]] begins to innoculate medical workers as part of a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19 following the arrival of the first 20,000 doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/instant-article/idUSL8N2KM77N (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] surpasses two million cases of COVID-19. [https://apnews.com/article/health-coronavirus-pandemic-latin-america-mexico-d8cc23f58571ef105313a2434d90ff32 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
****[[State of Palestine|Palestine]] reports their first cases of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] first detected in the [[United Kingdom]] in 139 people from the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/palestine-confirms-first-cases-of-coronavirus-strain/2146556 (Anadolu Agency)]
****[[Ministry of Health, Palestine|Health Minister]] [[Mai al-Kaila]] accuses [[Israel]] of blocking the delivery of 2,000 doses of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V vaccine]] to the [[Gaza Strip]], intended for [[Intensive care unit|ICU]] and emergency staff. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/16/israel-blocked-covid-vaccines-from-entering-gaza-say-palestinians (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[India]] reports their first four cases of the [[501.V2 variant]] from [[South Africa]] and one case of the [[Lineage P.1]] variant from [[Brazil]] in people who travelled internationally. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/south-african-covid-strain-detected-in-4-returnees-brazil-variant-in-one-says-government-2371788 (NDTV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] extends their [[Malaysian movement control order|movement control order]] in  [[Selangor]], [[Johor]] and [[Penang]] as well as the [[Federal territories of Malaysia|federal territory]] of [[Kuala Lumpur]] until March 4 but eases restrictions in other parts of the country. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-extends-mco-selangor-kl-johor-penang-feb-19-mar-4-14206236 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] signs an agreement with [[Novavax]] and [[Pfizer]] to secure additional doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for 23 million people in the second quarter of this year. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20210216001552315 (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[Morocco]] receives its second shipment of 500,000 doses of [[China]]'s [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/2809191/morocco-receives-second-batch-500000-sinopharm-doses (''Asharq Al-Awsat'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****The first batch consisting 80,000 doses of the [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] arrives at [[OR Tambo International Airport]] in [[Johannesburg]], which is unapproved for general use in [[South Africa]] and worldwide. [https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/first-batch-of-johnson-johnson-covid-19-vaccines-arrive-at-or-tambo-international-airport/ (SABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***The [[Therapeutic Goods Administration]] approves the emergency use of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by the [[University of Oxford]] and [[AstraZeneca]] for people over 18 years of age in [[Australia]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-16/coronavirus-astrazeneca-vaccine-approved-for-use-in-australia/13115784 (ABC Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]]ian [[Ministry of the Environment (Brazil)|Environment Minister]] [[Ricardo Salles]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2021/02/16/ministro-do-meio-ambiente-ricardo-salles-e-diagnosticado-com-covid-19-informa-assessoria.ghtml (G1)]
*The [[World Health Organization]] asks six [[Africa]]n countries ([[Senegal]], [[Guinea-Bissau]], [[Mali]], [[Ivory Coast]], [[Sierra Leone]] and [[Liberia]]) to be alert for possible [[Ebola]] outbreaks after [[Guinea]] and the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] reported new cases that signalled a resurgence of the outbreak. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/who-alerts-six-african-countries-after-ebola-outbreaks-here-s-the-list-101613484712633.html (''Hindustan Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
**The [[Myanmar Police Force]] files new charges against ousted [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|State Counsellor]] [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] for violating [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] regulations, which may allow her to be held indefinitely without trial. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/myanmar-police-new-charge-aung-san-suu-kyi/ (CBS News)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
**A lower court in [[The Hague]] orders the [[Government of the Netherlands|government]] to scrap its 9:00 pm to 4:30 am [[curfew]], citing violations of freedom of movement and assembly. [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]]'s government appealed the court decision, which was overturned by a high court. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/02/16/the-netherlands-must-lift-curfew-immediately-as-hague-ruling-says-government-response-ille (Euronews)]
*[[Capital punishment in Bangladesh]]
**A court in [[Bangladesh]] sentences five men [[capital punishment|to death]] for murdering Avijit Roy, an American-Bangladeshi blogger critical of [[religious extremism]], six years ago. The men belong to the [[al-Qaeda]]-inspired group [[Ansarullah Bangla Team]]. Another man was sentenced to life in prison. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/16/bangladesh-court-sentences-five-to-death-for-killing-us-blogger (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[NAACP]] and [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Bennie Thompson]] file a lawsuit accusing former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], Trump lawyer and former [[Mayor of New York City|New York City mayor]] [[Rudy Giuliani]], and [[Far-right politics|far-right]] groups such as the [[Proud Boys]] and [[Oath Keepers]] of conspiring to incite the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]]. The lawsuit, citing the [[Third Enforcement Act|Ku Klux Klan Act of 1871]], also accuses the defendants of disrupting the [[2021 United States Electoral College vote count|certification]] of Biden's victory by [[United States Congress|Congress]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/16/naacp-sues-trump-giuliani-of-conspiring-to-incite-capitol-riot.html (CNBC)]
**Christian Secor, a [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] student and founder of America First Bruins, is arrested by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] for sitting on the chair of former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] during the Capitol riot. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/legal-issues/ucla-student-arrest-capitol-riot/2021/02/17/e6f2394c-716f-11eb-b8a9-b9467510f0fe_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2020–2021 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Belarus]] authorities raid the offices of the [[Belarusian Association of Journalists|Association of Journalists]] and [[Viasna Human Rights Centre]] as part of the latest move to end protests against [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-belarus-journalists-18796f3a1b0e421cbfa1f18b3031786d (AP)]
*[[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] announces that there will be a probe following accusations of rape against his [[government of Australia|government]] in [[Parliament of Australia|Parliament]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/australianz/australian-pm-morrison-apologises-promises-probe-after-allegation-of-rape-in (''The Straits Times'')]
*Two men accused of leading a [[Christians|Christian]]-majority [[Anti-balaka]] group in the [[Central African Republic]] which targeted [[Muslim]]s plead not guilty at the start of their trial at the [[International Criminal Court]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-warcrimes-car/suspected-militia-leaders-plead-not-guilty-to-central-african-republic-war-crimes-idUSKBN2AG0ZT (Reuters)]
*Footage obtained by the [[BBC]] programme ''[[Panorama (British TV programme)|Panorama]]'' reveals that [[Emirate of Dubai|Dubai]] sheikha [[Latifa bint Mohammed Al Maktoum]] has been held in a private [[villa]] for at least a year after she attempted to escape from her family in February 2018. Latifa's close associates are calling for international intervention after they stopped receiving messages from her, fearing for her safety. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-56075528 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/16/secret-videos-raise-fears-for-princess-latifa-forcibly-returned-to-dubai (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2016 Philippine presidential election]]
**The [[Presidential Electoral Tribunal|Electoral Tribunal]] unanimously dismisses the electoral protest of former [[Senate of the Philippines|Senator]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] against [[Vice President of the Philippines|Vice President]] [[Leni Robredo]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1396382/pet-dismisses-marcos-poll-protest-vs-vp-leni-source (''The Philippine Daily Inquirer'')] [https://www.rappler.com/nation/supreme-court-junks-bongbong-marcos-protest-vs-leni-robredo (''Rappler'')]
*[[2019–20 Algerian protests]]
**Thousands of protestors defy [[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria|COVID-19 restrictions]] and take to the streets in [[Kherrata]] to both commemorate the second anniversary of the protests and to repeat their demands for the ruling government to step down. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/16/algeria-huge-rally-to-commemorate-protest-movement-anniversary (Al Jazeera)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}
